overlap.location_note: Savannah River 230 kV corridor near Hardeeville, SC / Purrysburg

known_costs.desc_cost_source: DESC 'Planned Transmission Projects $2M and Above' 5-Year Budget filing
known_costs.gpc_cost_note: Georgia Power's cost for this project is redacted as CEII in the public IRP filing. We do not estimate it; DESC's public cost is used only as a proxy for job scale.

illustrative_savings_estimate.assumption: mobilization = 3%-5% of contract cost, proxied by DESC's public $23,787,423 for this job
illustrative_savings_estimate.benchmark_source: Context: NYC DDC 2025 Utility Coordination Report found coordinated ('Joint Bidding') projects averaged ~$1.5M in utility-delay cost vs ~$5.8M for uncoordinated ones (~74% less). That is urban underground work, so we do not apply it directly; it only suggests our 3-5% mobilization-only figure is a floor, not a ceiling.

narrative: Jasper – Okatie 230 kV #2: Construct (DESC, $23,787,423, 6.5 mi of new 230 kV line, ~$3.7M/mi) and SAV: MCINTOSH - PURRYSBURG 230KV REACTORS (Georgia Power) are 5.65 mi apart and due 152 days apart. Both touch the same 230 kV corridor across the Savannah River near Hardeeville/Purrysburg, so they can share a staging yard, crews, equipment haul and, most importantly, one coordinated outage window, instead of each utility mobilizing separately. Avoiding one mobilization is worth roughly $0.7M-$1.2M before any shared right-of-way or outage-planning savings.
